clue.text: Produce uniform piece of low-down compost boxes

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the compost word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: manure is used as compost on gardens
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the low-down is inside information, and a fact is one piece of it

explanation.surface: A gardener's odd recipe: produce a uniform bit of muck that some compost encloses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' is the container signal; 'low-down' is slang for inside information, and one piece of it is a single fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to make goods, the verb sense of producing on a large scale.

clue.text: Some Embassy baggage returned in Gulf

indicators.note: returned means the run of letters taken is read backwards, as the clue is a down light
Some says only part of the words embassy baggage is used, a run straddling the two

explanation.surface: Diplomatic bags sent back from an embassy in the Gulf region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes SSYBA from embaSSY BAggage; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulf can be a deep chasm or wide gap, which is what an abyss is.

clue.text: Lift United with adulation

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football club names
adulation is lavish praise

explanation.surface: Fans lift a United player up, full of adulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up, or lift it, is an old verb sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Hermitage Museum's opening supporting a quiet artist

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the others, so it comes last

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the call for quiet
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of museum

explanation.surface: At the Hermitage Museum, the opening exhibit is a quiet artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hermitage' looks like the St Petersburg museum but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat, a place of seclusion like a hermit's dwelling.

clue.text: They pour from mountain fissures

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor
rents are tears or splits, so cracks or fissures

explanation.surface: Streams pour down from cracks in the mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are rushing floods of water, things that pour or stream down heavily.

clue.text: More chubby, almost game?

indicators.note: almost says the game's name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, a little like baseball

explanation.surface: Is a plumper player almost ready for the game?
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDERS is a British school game, similar to baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounder is the comparative of round, meaning plumper or more chubby in shape.

clue.text: Global warming expert's got coal limits resolved

indicators.note: resolved here means broken down and worked out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist has won agreement on capping coal use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges GOT COAL LIMITS; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies long-term weather patterns would be the kind of expert on rising world temperatures.

clue.text: Feeling conveyed that is not heartless

parts.note: conveyed means sent along
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: Emotion was conveyed, so it is not heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive and experience sensation, hence feeling as an adjective.

clue.text: One cared and isn't, I fancy, selfish

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, but here it signals the preceding letters made fanciful, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cared once and now doesn't, I think: how selfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ONE CARED ISNT I; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thoughtless of other people's feelings is selfish, a close synonym.

clue.text: Amateur Queen cover

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as in a layman
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An amateur performer playing the Queen needs a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a covering sheet or coat spread over a surface, like a coating.

clue.text: Massive star, practically perfect, embracing 'Posh'

indicators.note: practically means nearly, so the word for star loses its final letter

parts.note: a hero is the star of a story

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the word for perfect wraps around the next piece

parts.note: clean can mean flawless or perfect, as in a clean copy
U is the label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: A huge star, nearly flawless, dating a famous Spice Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' hints at Posh Spice, but is U, the upper-class label.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean, after the mythical strongman, means requiring or showing great strength, hence massive.

clue.text: 'Best friend' catching a cut branch to chew

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so the friend word encloses the rest

parts.note: mate is a close friend

indicators.note: cut says the word for branch loses its last letter

parts.note: a stick is a small branch off a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog grabs a broken branch to gnaw on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best friend' in quotes suggests man's best friend, a dog, chewing a stick; 'catching' signals the container and 'cut' drops a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to grind food in the mouth, the technical verb for chewing.

clue.text: Too much one would set back as before

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the joined letters are read backwards

parts.note: OTT stands for over the top, too much
I is the Roman numeral for one
'd is the short form of would, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Overdoing it would set anyone back, just like last time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to repeat what was said before.

clue.text: Sweet spot for drive outside below par

indicators.note: outside means the golf word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a tee is the spot a golfer drives from
feeling off means unwell, below par

explanation.surface: A golfer playing below par heads outside for a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below par' looks like golf scoring but means OFF, unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, one kind of sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Changing belief around when possible

indicators.note: around means the reworked letters go round the next piece
changing the word belief means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Changing one's belief becomes possible when the time comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges the letters into FEIBLE, which 'around' then wraps about the word for 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasible means practicable or able to be done, so possible.

clue.text: They ogle taking in finale of 'Buck Naked'

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the ogling word wraps the letter

parts.note: people who ogle are starers

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter, here of buck

explanation.surface: Gawpers flock to the climax of a show called Buck Naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for completely nude, from stark naked.

clue.text: More angry about Church beginning to roast witch

indicators.note: about means around, so the angry word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: sorer is more annoyed, as in sore meaning angry
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of roast

explanation.surface: The church grows angrier about the start of roasting a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: CE = Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a practitioner of magic, a male witch or wizard.

clue.text: Game of golf, par broken round course's last

indicators.note: round means the reworked letters go round the final piece
broken means the letters of golf par are smashed and reassembled
the last letter of course

explanation.surface: A golfer breaks par on a course's final hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the fodder into LAPFROG, and 'round' wraps that about the final letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game of vaulting over one another's backs.

clue.text: With oddly free site, the compiler's happy

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and every odd letter of free site

parts.note: the compiler's is the setter speaking: I have, written I've

explanation.surface: The setter is pleased with a strangely free venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes F, E, S, T from fReE SiTe; the setter calls themself 'the compiler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means jolly and celebratory, a cheerful, happy mood.

clue.text: Declared to be satisfied about Tories' leader

indicators.note: about means around, so the satisfied word goes round the letter

parts.note: sated means having had enough, satisfied

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Tories

explanation.surface: Content voters claim satisfaction with the Tory leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means said or announced formally, a close synonym of declared.

clue.text: Journey's special feature covering polar extremes

indicators.note: covering means the feature word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a trait is a distinctive feature
N and S are the north and south poles, the extremes of the globe

explanation.surface: A trip whose highlight takes in both ends of the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Journey' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the passage of people or goods from one place to another, a journey.

clue.text: Open container's finished

parts.note: a can is a metal container
did means completed, as in 'did the job'

explanation.surface: A container that has been opened and used up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and honest, the open sense of speaking freely.

clue.text: Girder's ends enclosed by small beams

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters, here of girder

parts.note: something enclosed is in
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A builder's picture: girder ends held in place by small beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like building timbers but is a verb: smiles broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to smile broadly, so beams as a verb matches broad smiles.

clue.text: Daily function, exterminator to be shown empty property

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day
to act is to operate or function

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the ends of exterminator

explanation.surface: A cleaner and pest-control man are shown round an empty house.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or 'char' is a British term for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a distinguishing quality, a property of something or someone.

clue.text: Part of chest or solid trunk

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choosing between a chest or a solid trunk for storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like luggage, alongside 'chest', but means the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the main part of the human body without head and limbs.

clue.text: Joined keeping unit and served in the army

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the joined word wraps the letter

parts.note: soldered means joined with molten metal
I is one, a unit

explanation.surface: A recruit joined a unit and did military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined' and 'unit' suggest enlisting, but SOLDERED is metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier is to serve as a soldier, so soldiered means served in the army.

clue.text: Sailor's capsizing holding head of pilot fish

indicators.note: holding means the overturned letters go round the next piece
capsizing means turning over, so the sailor's letters run backwards

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and with the 's it gives tar's

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of pilot

explanation.surface: A sailor's boat overturns while carrying a pilot fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' makes SRAT, and 'holding' puts P inside it. 'pilot fish' looks like one name, but 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small herring-like sea fish.

clue.text: Criminal raid — need top plunder

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of the next words are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A criminal gang plans a raid that needs a top-class haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges RAID NEED TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Depredation is the act of pillaging or ravaging, so plunder as a noun.
